title: Canonical composition of derived subsequence extensions
statement:
The composite derived left extensions along s in B_r and then r in B are canonically isomorphic to the derived extension along s.trans r. Its inverse followed by an arbitrary map has the transpose obtained by the two actual extension adjunctions followed by the exact restriction compositor.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u v w
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  [EssentiallySmall.{w} C]
  [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
  (S : SystemScalarAssignment (J := J)) (T : SystemTensorCoherence S)
  (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}) (r s : ℕ ↪o ℕ)
theorem systemSelectedDerivedComposition_mate
    (P : DerivedCategory (StrictRingSystem (selectedSystemRings B (s.trans r))))
    (M : DerivedCategory (StrictRingSystem B))
    (f : (systemSelectedDerivedExtension B r S T).derived.obj
      ((systemSelectedDerivedExtension (selectedSystemRings B r) s S T).derived.obj P) ⟶ M) :
    (systemSelectedDerivedExtension B (s.trans r) S T).adjunction.homEquiv P M
      ((systemSelectedDerivedComposition S T B r s).inv.app P ≫ f) =
    (systemSelectedDerivedExtension (selectedSystemRings B r) s S T).adjunction.homEquiv P
      ((derivedSystemSubsequence B r).obj M)
      ((systemSelectedDerivedExtension B r S T).adjunction.homEquiv _ M f) ≫
      (systemDerivedSubsequenceComposition B r s).hom.app M
```

proof.text: Transfer the composite adjunction along the canonical exact restriction compositor and take its left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism to the composite-selection adjunction. The inverse uniqueness map is the forward comparison for the reversed pair. Its Hom normalization identifies the transpose with the composite Hom equivalence; expanding that equivalence gives the stated mate formula.
